clusters.name: Replica Commit Coordination
clusters.description: Documents vary by the protocol and transaction mechanisms used to apply reference updates consistently across repository replicas.

relations.rationale: Three-phase commit makes update latency and throughput depend on every participating replica, constraining practical replication levels.
Coordinated reference transactions create a need to verify that replicas retain equivalent logical state.

values.label: Three-phase commit
values.description: Coordinates replica capability checks, tentative commit, and rollback for deterministic reference-update transactions.

values.label: Slowest-replica latency bound
values.description: Each coordination step waits for the slowest participating replica, limiting transaction performance as replica groups grow.

values.label: Replica-count scaling bottleneck
values.description: Increasing the number of replicas reduces push throughput under three-phase commit.

clusters.name: Replication Factor
clusters.description: Documents vary by the number of repository replicas selected to balance redundancy, capacity, consistency, and continued write availability.

relations.rationale: The selected replication factor determines how many participants three-phase commit must coordinate.
Maintaining write availability during maintenance depends on retaining enough replicas to form a quorum.

values.label: Three replicas per repository
values.description: Uses three replicas to provide redundancy and tolerate one machine failure while accepting pushes.

values.label: Three-replica minimum
values.description: Keeps three replicas even for small repositories to preserve consistency and reduce data-loss risk.

values.label: Replication floor and capacity ceiling
values.description: The fixed replication floor is costly for small repositories while offering insufficient serving capacity for massive repositories.

clusters.name: Replica State Verification
clusters.description: Documents vary by how systems detect or establish equivalence among replicated repository states after reference updates.

relations.rationale: Replica commit coordination produces state whose post-update equivalence must be checked independently.

values.label: Spokes checksum
values.description: Summarizes reference names, values, and replica state to compare logical contents across replicas.

values.label: Incremental XOR checksum maintenance
values.description: Updates checksum contributions when references change instead of rescanning the complete reference set.

values.label: Full checksum recomputation
values.description: Recomputing all reference hashes from scratch becomes expensive for repositories with many references.

values.label: Reference-update throughput constraint
values.description: The cost of full recomputation would limit the achievable rate of reference updates.

clusters.name: Repository Authority Model
clusters.description: Documents vary by where authoritative repository state resides and whether serving nodes require fixed per-repository ownership.

relations.rationale: Stateless serving requires a routing mechanism that can locate or recreate repositories without authoritative placement records.
S3 compare-and-swap serialization enables any server to receive updates without fixed-primary consensus.

values.label: S3-backed write-ahead log
values.description: Stores authoritative repository state in S3 rather than on a particular serving server.

values.label: Stateless repository-serving cluster
values.description: Treats local repository copies as replaceable warm caches and avoids authoritative server-local repository state.

values.label: Consensus-free repository primaries
values.description: Allows any server to receive updates instead of using elections or fixed primary ownership.

values.label: S3 compare-and-swap synchronization
values.description: Uses atomic S3 compare-and-swap operations to serialize concurrent write-ahead-log updates.

clusters.name: Repository Placement Strategy
clusters.description: Documents vary by how requests locate repositories and how missing local materializations are recovered across a changing server cluster.

relations.rationale: Placement can remain non-authoritative because repository state is recoverable from the S3-backed source of truth.

values.label: Rendezvous-hashed repository placement
values.description: Maps repository identifiers to expected nodes without maintaining authoritative placement state.

values.label: Repository-ID and healthy-node routing
values.description: Uses only the repository ID and current healthy-node set, tolerating stale routing because repositories can be rematerialized.

values.label: Warm-cache materialization
values.description: Recreates absent local repositories from the S3 write-ahead log when routing directs work to another node.

values.label: Rendezvous-ranked preferred primary
values.description: Normally favors the highest-ranked node to reduce compare-and-swap retries while allowing other servers during failures.

clusters.name: Maintenance Transition Strategy
clusters.description: Documents vary by how servers enter planned maintenance while preserving active reads and continued replicated writes.

relations.rationale: Quiescent maintenance depends on sufficient remaining replicas to continue quorum-based writes.
The maintenance procedure reuses replica coordination behavior while withdrawing a server from new reads.

values.label: Direct reboot or unplugging
values.description: Stops a server immediately, risking interruption and loss of progress for long-running reads such as large clones.

values.label: Quiescing period
values.description: Withdraws a server from new reads while allowing active operations to drain before reboot.

values.label: Continued write delivery during quiescence
values.description: Continues sending writes to the quiescing replica so it does not fall arbitrarily behind.

values.label: Long and variable quiescence duration
values.description: Maintenance duration may range from seconds to hours because active reads, especially large clones, are allowed to finish.

clusters.name: Client Maintenance Execution
clusters.description: Documents vary by whether repository fetching and graph maintenance occur in foreground commands or asynchronously in the background.

relations.rationale: The documented background maintenance mechanisms are delivered through Scalar's client-side repository management layer.

values.label: Background repository fetching
values.description: Fetches objects periodically outside foreground commands to reduce perceived user waiting.

values.label: Hidden remote-reference namespace
values.description: Stores background-fetched references under a separate namespace without changing ordinary local or remote-tracking refs.

values.label: Background split commit-graph maintenance
values.description: Updates reachable commit graphs incrementally in the background to preserve large-repository performance.

values.label: Foreground fetch overhead
values.description: Commit-graph generation during foreground fetches adds work and user-visible waiting.

values.label: Reduced foreground command waiting
values.description: Background object and graph maintenance shifts expensive work away from commands for which users are waiting.

clusters.name: Client Scaling Integration
clusters.description: Documents vary by whether large-repository performance is supplied by an auxiliary client layer or absorbed into core Git.

relations.rationale: Scalar registration and background maintenance provide the operational mechanism for the documented client-side scaling behavior.

values.label: Custom Git build dependency
values.description: Requires a Git build containing Scalar-specific functionality for repository-scaling features.

values.label: Scalar performance layer
values.description: Uses Scalar as an additional client mechanism for achieving required large-repository performance.

values.label: Core Git performance capabilities
values.description: Moves repository management and performance features into the core Git client.

values.label: Additional Git management layers
values.description: The longer-term design rejects continued dependence on management layers such as Scalar above core Git.

values.label: Scalar-to-core-Git transition
values.description: Treats Scalar as a transitional solution while equivalent capabilities become available in core Git.

values.description: Treats local repository copies as replaceable warm caches and avoids authoritative server-local repository state.

values.label: RPC-based repository access
values.description: Accessing repositories remotely through an application-facing RPC layer.

values.label: Dedicated repository fileservers
values.description: Storing repositories on dedicated fileservers rather than a shared distributed filesystem.

values.label: Single-machine repository storage
values.description: Keeping each repository on only one machine after remote fileserver access.

values.label: Co-located GVFS cache server
values.description: Places a cache server with the repository to handle many GVFS protocol requests.

values.label: Git protocol with Scalar registration
values.description: Uses ordinary Git protocol and client registration when GVFS cache infrastructure is unavailable.

values.label: GVFS without cache server
values.description: Uses GVFS protocol without a dedicated cache server for repositories small enough not to require one.

values.label: Git hosting operational difficulty
values.description: Makes repository hosting operations a significant scalability and reliability concern.

clusters.name: Client Clone Materialization
clusters.description: How are repository content and working-tree data materialized on large-repository clients?

values.label: Partial-clone object materialization
values.description: Fetching missing repository objects on demand instead of storing every reachable object locally.

values.label: Virtualized filesystem materialization
values.description: Using a virtualized filesystem to support very large repositories without fully materializing content.

values.label: Sparse-checkout materialization
values.description: Populating only selected working-tree paths to control client materialization size.

values.label: GVFS-protocol cloning
values.description: Cloning through the GVFS hosting protocol for large repositories.

values.label: Virtualized filesystem materialization
values.description: Using a virtualized filesystem to support very large repositories without fully materializing content.

values.label: Nested source working directory
values.description: Places the working tree beneath the repository directory to separate source files from adjacent build outputs.

values.label: Sibling build-output directories
values.description: Keeps build outputs outside the working directory while retaining a nested source layout.

values.label: Reduced Git working-directory management load
values.description: Separating build outputs from the working directory reduces the work Git performs while managing repository files.

clusters.name: Repository Storage Representation
clusters.description: Which storage representation and access pattern supports repository object workloads at scale?

values.label: Size-minimizing packfile layout
values.description: Organizing packed objects primarily to minimize storage size, accepting physical indirection and random reads.

values.label: Whole-file local caching
values.description: Caching an entire repository file locally to make random access acceptable.

values.label: Distributed filesystem architecture
values.description: Distributing repository storage through a shared filesystem.

values.label: Plain Git repositories on local NVMe
values.description: Stores ordinary Git repositories on local NVMe to support random packfile reads and standard client access.

values.label: Normal on-disk Git repository operations
values.description: Runs standard Git operations against ordinary on-disk repositories using upstream-compatible tooling.

values.label: Eventually consistent repository replicas
values.description: Allows replicas to expose newly pushed repository data only after propagation completes.

values.label: Efficient Git cloning
values.description: Preserves efficient cloning by retaining plain Git data rather than transforming it for clients.

clusters.name: Replica Failure Recovery
clusters.description: How are failed or retiring replica servers detected and repaired to restore repository redundancy?

values.label: Live-traffic-based failure detection
values.description: Detecting server failure from live application traffic and routing requests around unavailable servers.

values.label: Automated permanent-failure repair
values.description: Automatically restoring repository replication after disk or server failures.

values.label: Retiring-server replica-count removal
values.description: Removing a retiring server from active replica counts while keeping it available until repairs complete.

clusters.name: Version-Control Operating Model
clusters.description: Which collaboration and repository-control model governs how users and teams exchange Git changes?

values.label: Distributed version-control model
values.description: Retains decentralized repositories and offline change exchange as the underlying version-control model.

values.label: Decentralized subsystem-maintainer workflow
values.description: Organizes development through many maintainers and decentralized subsystem ownership.

values.label: Offline work and delayed-push capabilities
values.description: Provides offline development and postpones synchronization with the central host.

values.label: Distributed-model mismatch with centralized workflows
values.description: Creates friction when organizations use centralized coordination rather than decentralized development.

values.label: Centralized repository hosting
values.description: Coordinates users through a centralized repository host despite distributed client capabilities.

clusters.name: Replica Commit Coordination
clusters.description: Documents vary by the protocol and transaction mechanisms used to apply reference updates consistently across repository replicas.

relations.rationale: Coordinated reference transactions create a need to verify that replicas retain equivalent logical state.

values.label: Three-phase commit
values.description: Coordinates replica capability checks, tentative commit, and rollback for deterministic reference-update transactions.

values.label: Slowest-replica latency bound
values.description: Each coordination step waits for the slowest participating replica, limiting transaction performance as replica groups grow.

values.label: Replica-count scaling bottleneck
values.description: Increasing the number of replicas reduces push throughput under three-phase commit.

values.label: Consensus-free repository primaries
values.description: Allows any server to receive updates instead of using elections or fixed primary ownership.

values.label: Majority-based write commitment
values.description: Committing writes after a replica majority, with at least two replicas producing the same state.

values.label: Application-level repository replication
values.description: Applying repository replication in an application-level system rather than filesystem replication.

values.label: Git-and-rsync replication mechanisms
values.description: Combining Git and rsync mechanisms to replicate repository content.

values.label: Coalesced bookkeeping reference updates
values.description: Combining non-time-critical bookkeeping reference updates into fewer transactions.

values.label: Priority scheduling for user-initiated updates
values.description: Prioritizing user reference updates over bookkeeping updates during cascades.

values.label: Non-voting geo-replication replicas
values.description: Keeping geographically replicated hosts out of write-voting quorums so writes survive their temporary unavailability.

values.label: Reduced update-cascade request delay
values.description: Reducing user-request delay during large bookkeeping reference-update cascades.

values.label: High-latency reference-update constraint
values.description: Limiting reference-update throughput because distant replica coordination incurs high latency.

values.label: Internal reference-update amplification
values.description: Generating many bookkeeping reference updates from one user push or pull-request workflow.

values.label: Reference-update latency budget
values.description: Restricting each reference update to a few hundred milliseconds to sustain repository throughput.

values.label: Read-dominant repository workload
values.description: Operating under a workload with roughly one hundred reads per write.

values.label: Global push linearization
values.description: Orders all pushes into one deterministic operation history for repository consistency.

values.label: Consensus-based repository replication
values.description: Uses consensus coordination to keep multiple repository copies consistent during pushes.

values.label: Orchestrated packfile fan-out
values.description: Distributes pushed packfiles to every repository instance before references are published.

values.label: Unsynchronized packfile distribution
values.description: Fans out unreachable packfiles without consensus, relying on later synchronized reference commitment.

values.label: Git reference transaction locking
values.description: Locks and verifies references until a distributed transaction commits or aborts.

values.label: Packfile-level replication
values.description: Replicates Git data as packfiles while leaving Git operations standard on each repository replica.

values.label: Fully consistent replica synchronization
values.description: Keeps replicated Git data synchronized so clients and CI can immediately read newly pushed commits.

values.label: Repository-consistency complexity cost
values.description: Incurs substantial operational complexity to keep repository copies fully synchronized.

values.label: Repository copies as consensus source
values.description: What repository state establishes consensus for replicated operations?

clusters.name: Replica Checksum Strategy
clusters.description: Which checksum implementation verifies equivalence among replicated repository states?

relations.rationale: Replica commit coordination produces state whose post-update equivalence must be checked independently.

values.label: Spokes checksum
values.description: Summarizes reference names, values, and replica state to compare logical contents across replicas.

values.label: Incremental XOR checksum maintenance
values.description: Updates checksum contributions when references change instead of rescanning the complete reference set.

values.label: Full checksum recomputation
values.description: Recomputing all reference hashes from scratch becomes expensive for repositories with many references.

values.label: Reference-update throughput constraint
values.description: The cost of full recomputation would limit the achievable rate of reference updates.

clusters.name: Repository Placement Strategy
clusters.description: Documents vary by how requests locate repositories and how missing local materializations are recovered across a changing server cluster.

values.label: Rendezvous-hashed repository placement
values.description: Maps repository identifiers to expected nodes without maintaining authoritative placement state.

values.label: Repository-ID and healthy-node routing
values.description: Uses only the repository ID and current healthy-node set, tolerating stale routing because repositories can be rematerialized.

values.label: Warm-cache materialization
values.description: Recreates absent local repositories from the S3 write-ahead log when routing directs work to another node.

values.label: Rendezvous-ranked preferred primary
values.description: Normally favors the highest-ranked node to reduce compare-and-swap retries while allowing other servers during failures.

values.label: Any-replica read routing
values.description: Routes fetches and clones to any synchronized replica instead of a designated read replica.

values.label: Routing-database availability dependency
values.description: What dependency is introduced by storing repository-to-machine placement in an external routing database?

clusters.name: Maintenance Transition Strategy
clusters.description: Documents vary by how servers enter planned maintenance while preserving active reads and continued replicated writes.

relations.rationale: The maintenance procedure reuses replica coordination behavior while withdrawing a server from new reads.

values.label: Direct reboot or unplugging
values.description: Stops a server immediately, risking interruption and loss of progress for long-running reads such as large clones.

values.label: Quiescing period
values.description: Withdraws a server from new reads while allowing active operations to drain before reboot.

values.label: Continued write delivery during quiescence
values.description: Continues sending writes to the quiescing replica so it does not fall arbitrarily behind.

values.label: Long and variable quiescence duration
values.description: Maintenance duration may range from seconds to hours because active reads, especially large clones, are allowed to finish.

values.label: Rolling reboot testing
values.description: Tests failures through planned rack-scoped rolling reboots rather than random interruption.

values.label: Rack-scoped availability-zone maintenance
values.description: Reboots one rack at a time and bounds simultaneous reboots within that rack.

values.label: Bounded parallel server reboots
values.description: Limits concurrent reboots after quiescence to control maintenance disruption.

values.label: Increased same-day write-rejection risk
values.description: Reduced replication after sudden loss increases the chance that later writes are rejected.

clusters.name: Client Maintenance Execution
clusters.description: Documents vary by whether repository fetching and graph maintenance occur in foreground commands or asynchronously in the background.

relations.rationale: The documented background maintenance mechanisms are delivered through Scalar's client-side repository management layer.

values.description: Fetches objects periodically outside foreground commands to reduce perceived user waiting.

values.label: Hidden remote-reference namespace
values.description: Stores background-fetched references under a separate namespace without changing ordinary local or remote-tracking refs.

values.label: Background split commit-graph maintenance
values.description: Updates reachable commit graphs incrementally in the background to preserve large-repository performance.

values.label: Foreground fetch overhead
values.description: Commit-graph generation during foreground fetches adds work and user-visible waiting.

values.label: Reduced foreground command waiting
values.description: Background object and graph maintenance shifts expensive work away from commands for which users are waiting.

values.label: Updated Git index format
values.description: Using a compact index representation to reduce large-repository client command overhead.

values.label: Git-aware filesystem watcher
values.description: Using a Git-specific watcher to avoid broad filesystem scans during client maintenance.

values.label: Watchman filesystem watching
values.description: Using the general-purpose Watchman watcher for client filesystem change detection.

values.label: Untracked cache
values.description: Caching untracked-file information to reduce working-directory inspection work.

values.label: Separate fetch-objects endpoint
values.description: Downloading pack files through a separate endpoint while central services control branch updates.

values.label: Index-file size reduction
values.description: Reducing the large-repository index file from 400 MB to 250 MB.

values.label: Single-file Git index storage
values.description: Maintaining tracked paths in one index file read and written by core commands.

values.label: Background Git maintenance
values.description: Running repository maintenance asynchronously instead of periodic foreground garbage collection.

values.label: Performance bottleneck tracing
values.description: Using custom traces and user feedback to identify large-repository client bottlenecks.

values.description: Applies supported Git settings asynchronously to registered repositories after installation.

values.label: Disabled automatic garbage collection
values.description: Disables command-triggered garbage collection so cleanup runs through background maintenance.

values.label: Disabled ahead-behind status calculation
values.description: Omits potentially expensive branch-divergence computation during status operations.

values.label: Watchman-based filesystem monitoring hook
values.description: Uses a Watchman-connected filesystem-monitoring hook to accelerate Git status-related operations.

values.label: Single-command maintenance execution
values.description: Runs configuration, fetching, graph updates, and object cleanup together through one maintenance command.

values.label: Automatic enlistment registration during cloning
values.description: Registers newly cloned repositories automatically for recommended configuration and maintenance.

values.label: Foreground maintenance execution
values.description: Allows operators to run repository maintenance manually on demand alongside scheduled background work.

values.label: Scalar performance layer
values.description: Uses Scalar as an additional client mechanism for achieving required large-repository performance.

values.label: Core Git performance capabilities
values.description: Moves repository management and performance features into the core Git client.

values.label: Additional Git management layers
values.description: The longer-term design rejects continued dependence on management layers such as Scalar above core Git.

values.label: Scalar-to-core-Git transition
values.description: Treats Scalar as a transitional solution while equivalent capabilities become available in core Git.

values.label: Scalar configuration tuning
values.description: Applying recommended Git configuration values to accelerate client commands.

values.label: GVFS Protocol in standard Git
values.description: Is the GVFS Protocol integrated into the standard Git client?

values.description: Placing repository replicas in different racks to isolate rack-wide failures.

values.description: Placing replicas across geographically separated locations despite inter-replica latency.

values.description: Keeping filesystem replicas near one another because block replication is latency-sensitive.

values.label: Block-level filesystem replication
values.description: Replicating repository storage at filesystem or block level.

values.label: Geographically localized replica reads
values.description: Serving reads from synchronized replicas near users to improve transfer locality.

values.label: Durable highly available content access
values.description: Maintaining durable, highly available repository and gist access through multi-copy replication.

values.label: Geographically localized Git transfer serving
values.description: Improving Git transfer speed by serving reads from nearby synchronized replicas.

values.label: Three replicas per repository
values.description: Maintaining three repository copies as the selected replication factor.

values.label: Replication floor and capacity ceiling
values.description: The fixed replication floor is costly for small repositories while offering insufficient serving capacity for massive repositories.

values.label: Two-copy repository state after sudden loss

values.description: Persisting authoritative repository updates through a write-ahead log in S3.

values.label: Push acknowledgment after WAL persistence
values.description: Acknowledges pushes only after their complete operation is durable in the authoritative log.

values.label: Fully consistent repository views
values.description: Maintains every accessed repository view as fully consistent rather than partially consistent.

values.label: External relational database for repository references

values.label: Core Git performance capabilities

values.label: Reliability-performance-scale platform objectives

values.label: Low-friction platform migration

values.label: Incremental infrastructure evolution
values.description: Version-control infrastructure continues evolving as workload and platform conditions change.

values.label: Agent-driven workload growth

values.label: Repository availability productivity impact
values.description: Repository unavailability directly reduces developer and CI productivity.

clusters.name: Replica Topology and Factor
clusters.description: How many replicas and what physical topology provide repository redundancy and failure isolation?

values.label: Rack-level replica anti-colocation
values.description: Placing repository replicas in different racks to isolate rack-wide failures.

values.label: Distant replica placement
values.description: Placing replicas across geographically separated locations despite inter-replica latency.

values.label: Colocated filesystem replicas
values.description: Keeping filesystem replicas near one another because block replication is latency-sensitive.

values.label: Block-level filesystem replication
values.description: Replicating repository storage at filesystem or block level.

values.label: Geographically localized replica reads
values.description: Serving reads from synchronized replicas near users to improve transfer locality.

values.label: Durable highly available content access
values.description: Maintaining durable, highly available repository and gist access through multi-copy replication.

values.label: Geographically localized Git transfer serving
values.description: Improving Git transfer speed by serving reads from nearby synchronized replicas.

values.label: Three replicas per repository
values.description: Maintaining three repository copies as the selected replication factor.

values.label: Replication floor and capacity ceiling
values.description: The fixed replication floor is costly for small repositories while offering insufficient serving capacity for massive repositories.

values.label: Two-copy repository state after sudden loss
values.description: Leaves a repository with two surviving copies after an unexpected server disappearance, preserving service but reducing failure tolerance.

values.label: Non-voting geo-replication replicas
values.description: Keeping geographically replicated hosts out of write-voting quorums so writes survive their temporary unavailability.

values.label: Elastic per-repository replica allocation
values.description: Replica counts vary with repository demand, from minimal availability to large read-serving pools.

clusters.name: Authority Synchronization
clusters.description: Which mechanism coordinates authoritative repository state persistence and synchronization?

values.label: S3-backed write-ahead log
values.description: Persisting authoritative repository updates through a write-ahead log in S3.

values.label: S3 compare-and-swap synchronization
values.description: Uses atomic S3 compare-and-swap operations to serialize concurrent write-ahead-log updates.

values.label: WAL-based repository consistency
values.description: Uses a write-ahead log as the authoritative record for consistent repository operations without an external relational database.

values.label: Push acknowledgment after WAL persistence
values.description: Acknowledges pushes only after their complete operation is durable in the authoritative log.

values.label: Fully consistent repository views
values.description: Maintains every accessed repository view as fully consistent rather than partially consistent.

values.label: External relational database for repository references
values.description: Stores repository references in an external relational database alongside blob-stored packfiles.

values.label: Consensus-free repository primaries
values.description: Allows any server to receive updates instead of using elections or fixed primary ownership.

values.label: Repository copies as consensus source
values.description: What repository state establishes consensus for replicated operations?

values.label: Cloud-agnostic object-storage deployment
values.description: The authority log runs on S3-compatible object storage across cloud providers.

values.label: Batched WAL uploads
values.description: Multiple pushes are grouped to avoid one object-store write per push.

values.label: One-object-store-write-per-push ingestion
values.description: Each push is ingested with a separate object-store write.

values.label: Single-local-repository reference synchronization
values.description: Reference transactions synchronize with one local repository instead of a replica quorum.

values.label: Periodic WAL compaction
values.description: The write-ahead log is periodically compacted to bound restore cost and retained history.

values.label: Compaction results recorded across storage representations
values.description: Compaction outcomes are recorded for both the WAL and on-disk repository so replicas reproduce them.

values.label: S3 Express One Zone deployment
values.description: High-performance clusters use a lower-latency object-storage tier for WAL updates and push ingestion.

values.label: ETag-conditional read verification
values.description: Replicas use conditional object-storage reads to verify WAL-index freshness before serving fetches or clones.

clusters.name: Repository Serving Architecture

values.label: Stateless repository-serving cluster
values.description: Treats local repository copies as replaceable warm caches and avoids authoritative server-local repository state.

values.label: RPC-based repository access
values.description: Accessing repositories remotely through an application-facing RPC layer.

values.label: Dedicated repository fileservers
values.description: Storing repositories on dedicated fileservers rather than a shared distributed filesystem.

values.label: Single-machine repository storage
values.description: Keeping each repository on only one machine after remote fileserver access.

values.label: Co-located GVFS cache server
values.description: Places a cache server with the repository to handle many GVFS protocol requests.

values.label: Git protocol with Scalar registration
values.description: Uses ordinary Git protocol and client registration when GVFS cache infrastructure is unavailable.

values.label: GVFS without cache server
values.description: Uses GVFS protocol without a dedicated cache server for repositories small enough not to require one.

values.label: Git hosting operational difficulty
values.description: Makes repository hosting operations a significant scalability and reliability concern.

values.label: Horizontal application-server replication
values.description: How does the serving application scale its application instances around repository access?

values.label: Warm-cache materialization
values.description: Recreates absent local repositories from the S3 write-ahead log when routing directs work to another node.

clusters.name: Client Clone Materialization
clusters.description: How are repository content and working-tree data materialized on large-repository clients?

values.label: Partial-clone object materialization
values.description: Fetching missing repository objects on demand instead of storing every reachable object locally.

values.label: Virtualized filesystem materialization
values.description: Using a virtualized filesystem to support very large repositories without fully materializing content.

values.label: Sparse-checkout materialization
values.description: Populating only selected working-tree paths to control client materialization size.

values.label: GVFS-protocol cloning
values.description: Cloning through the GVFS hosting protocol for large repositories.

values.label: Virtualized filesystem materialization
values.description: Using a virtualized filesystem to support very large repositories without fully materializing content.

values.label: Nested source working directory
values.description: Places the working tree beneath the repository directory to separate source files from adjacent build outputs.

values.label: Sibling build-output directories
values.description: Keeps build outputs outside the working directory while retaining a nested source layout.

values.label: Reduced Git working-directory management load
values.description: Separating build outputs from the working directory reduces the work Git performs while managing repository files.

values.label: Reduced object-transfer burden
values.description: Partial transfer and caching reduce client data movement and central-server load compared with complete object database transfer.

values.label: Populated-file data cost
values.description: Populating working files costs substantially more data movement and processing than changing index entries.

values.label: Populated-file modification-detection cost
values.description: Determining modifications across many populated files becomes an important client scalability cost.

clusters.name: Repository Storage Representation
clusters.description: Which repository object representation and access pattern supports server-scale Git workloads?

values.label: Size-minimizing packfile layout
values.description: Organizing packed objects primarily to minimize storage size, accepting physical indirection and random reads.

values.label: Whole-file local caching
values.description: Caching an entire repository file locally to make random access acceptable.

values.label: Distributed filesystem architecture
values.description: Distributing repository storage through a shared filesystem.

values.label: Plain Git repositories on local NVMe
values.description: Stores ordinary Git repositories on local NVMe to support random packfile reads and standard client access.

values.label: Normal on-disk Git repository operations
values.description: Runs standard Git operations against ordinary on-disk repositories using upstream-compatible tooling.

values.label: Eventually consistent repository replicas
values.description: Allows replicas to expose newly pushed repository data only after propagation completes.

values.label: Efficient Git cloning
values.description: Preserves efficient cloning by retaining plain Git data rather than transforming it for clients.

values.label: Network-filesystem performance and correctness problems
values.description: What operational effect results when Git repositories are exposed through networked filesystem semantics?

values.label: Content-addressable object storage
values.description: Repository objects are stored and addressed by content hashes.

values.label: DAG-dependent object traversal
values.description: Repository access follows dependent commit, tree, and file references sequentially.

values.label: Distributed key-value object storage
values.description: Git objects are mapped directly onto a distributed key-value store.

values.label: Distributed hash-table packfile storage
values.description: Normal on-disk packfiles are replaced by a distributed hash table.

values.label: Packfile-based network transfer
values.description: Git transfers repository changes through packfiles over the network.

values.label: Distributed-store access overhead
values.description: Object-level distributed storage adds repeated network round trips and latency.

values.label: Unacceptable clone performance
values.description: Object-level distribution makes repository cloning too slow for practical use.

values.label: Distributed identical repository instances
values.description: Hosting servers and developer machines retain the same distributed repository model.

values.label: Packfile-based repository storage
values.description: Repository code and metadata are stored in compressed filesystem packfiles.

values.label: Single on-disk HTTP repository
values.description: An HTTP daemon serves one local on-disk repository.

values.label: Server-internal non-packfile storage
values.description: The server uses an internal representation other than packfiles while preserving packfile network operations.

values.label: Multi-machine repository placement
values.description: Repository data is distributed across multiple disks and machines for parallelism and availability.

values.label: Packfile hosting management burden
values.description: Large binary packfiles make filesystem-scale repository management difficult.

values.label: Packfile hosting scalability ceiling
values.description: Packfile-based hosting limits availability and scalability for large providers.

clusters.name: Packfile Lifecycle Management
clusters.description: How are Git packfiles repacked, indexed, retained, and removed over time?

values.label: Incremental pack-file repacking
values.description: Which pack-maintenance strategy limits each repacking operation while reducing large repositories’ pack count?

values.label: Multi-pack-index reference redirection
values.description: Which index mechanism redirects selected objects to newly generated packs while retaining old packs temporarily?

values.label: Deferred obsolete-pack deletion
values.description: When are obsolete pack files deleted relative to pack creation and reference updates?

values.label: Unbounded pack-file accumulation
values.description: What pack-growth condition can result when pack maintenance is not bounded?

values.label: Pack-count and storage-footprint reduction
values.description: What storage result follows from incremental repacking and obsolete-pack expiration?

values.label: Single-pack-file repacking
values.description: Accumulated packfiles are rewritten into one packfile as a maintenance strategy unsuitable for very large repositories.

values.label: Primary-only compaction
values.description: Only the primary replica performs repository compaction, while replicas consume the recorded result.

values.label: Replica-side repository repacking
values.description: Replicas independently trigger repository repacking as opposed to consuming primary-produced compacted data.

values.label: Git compaction as ingestion bottleneck
values.description: At high throughput, on-disk Git compaction becomes the limiting factor for repository ingestion.

clusters.name: Replica Failure Recovery
clusters.description: How are failed or retiring replica servers detected and repaired to restore repository redundancy?

values.label: Live-traffic-based failure detection
values.description: Detecting server failure from live application traffic and routing requests around unavailable servers.

values.label: Automated permanent-failure repair
values.description: Automatically restoring repository replication after disk or server failures.

values.label: Retiring-server replica-count removal
values.description: Removing a retiring server from active replica counts while keeping it available until repairs complete.

values.label: MxN failure-detection matrix
values.description: How are failure observations distributed across application servers and file servers?

values.label: Per-application-server failure isolation
values.description: How are failure classifications isolated when one application server has a local connectivity or DNS fault?

values.label: Localized failure-detector false positive
values.description: What failure-detection error can remain localized to one application server?

values.label: Heartbeat-based primary failure detection
values.description: Which mechanism is used as the primary detector for failed repository servers?

values.label: Advisory replica-offline status
values.description: How is an uncertain offline judgment represented in replica routing?

values.label: Cross-server fault inference
values.description: How are file-server faults distinguished from application-server faults?

values.label: Pet-style repository operations
values.description: Are repositories managed as individually irreplaceable assets or interchangeable instances?

values.label: Operational burden of repository health management
values.description: What operational effect follows from continuous repository location, checksum, corruption, and repair management?

values.label: Three-consecutive-failure offline threshold
values.description: A replica is marked offline only after three consecutive request failures.

values.label: Losing-replica isolation
values.description: Replicas on the losing side of a write vote are removed from reads and writes until repaired.

values.label: N-to-N replica reconstruction
values.description: Replacement replicas can be created anywhere from either surviving repository copy.

values.label: Cluster-size recovery scaling
values.description: Replica recovery accelerates as the file-server cluster grows.

values.label: Replica failover from concurrent maintenance
values.description: Concurrent maintenance on multiple replica nodes can trigger repository failover and availability impact.

clusters.name: Version-Control Operating Model
clusters.description: Which collaboration and repository-control model governs how users and teams exchange Git changes?

values.label: Distributed version-control model
values.description: Retains decentralized repositories and offline change exchange as the underlying version-control model.

values.label: Decentralized subsystem-maintainer workflow
values.description: Organizes development through many maintainers and decentralized subsystem ownership.

values.label: Offline work and delayed-push capabilities
values.description: Provides offline development and postpones synchronization with the central host.

values.label: Distributed-model mismatch with centralized workflows
values.description: Creates friction when organizations use centralized coordination rather than decentralized development.

values.label: Centralized repository hosting
values.description: Coordinates users through a centralized repository host despite distributed client capabilities.

values.label: Central-server-coupled object retrieval
values.description: Clients rely on a central server for missing objects, relaxing the fully distributed collaboration model.

clusters.name: Replica Commit Coordination
clusters.description: Which coordination mechanism orders and publishes updates across repository replicas?

relations.rationale: Coordinated reference transactions create a need to verify that replicas retain equivalent logical state.

values.label: Three-phase commit
values.description: Coordinates replica capability checks, tentative commit, and rollback for deterministic reference-update transactions.

values.label: Majority-based write commitment
values.description: Committing writes after a replica majority, with at least two replicas producing the same state.

values.label: Consensus-based repository replication
values.description: Uses consensus coordination to keep multiple repository copies consistent during pushes.

values.label: Git reference transaction locking
values.description: Locks and verifies references until a distributed transaction commits or aborts.

values.label: Global push linearization
values.description: Orders all pushes into one deterministic operation history for repository consistency.

values.label: Per-write voting protocol
values.description: Each write independently determines its winning order and commitment outcome.

values.label: Overlapped coordinator work during network waits
values.description: The coordinator performs locking, checksumming, and reads concurrently with network operations.

clusters.name: Replica Write Commitment Policy
clusters.description: Which consistency, durability, and availability policy determines when replicated writes are accepted or rolled back?

relations.rationale: Coordinated reference transactions create a need to verify that replicas retain equivalent logical state.

values.label: Reduced update-cascade request delay
values.description: Reducing user-request delay during large bookkeeping reference-update cascades.

values.label: High-latency reference-update constraint
values.description: Limiting reference-update throughput because distant replica coordination incurs high latency.

values.label: Internal reference-update amplification
values.description: Generating many bookkeeping reference updates from one user push or pull-request workflow.

values.label: Reference-update latency budget
values.description: Restricting each reference update to a few hundred milliseconds to sustain repository throughput.

values.label: Minority-write rollback
values.description: Writes lacking majority agreement are reverted on replicas where they were applied.

values.label: Consistency and partition-tolerance priority
values.description: Replication preserves consistency and partition tolerance even when unrestricted availability is sacrificed.

values.label: Insufficient-replication write refusal
values.description: Writes are refused when the minimum number of durable copies cannot be created.

values.label: Durability-before-write-availability policy
values.description: Write availability is sacrificed to prevent permanent data loss.

values.label: Availability-durability separation
values.description: Serving requests and preserving accepted writes are treated as distinct resilience properties.

values.label: Slowest-replica latency bound
values.description: Each coordination step waits for the slowest participating replica, limiting transaction performance as replica groups grow.

clusters.name: Repository Replication Mechanism
clusters.description: Which mechanism distributes repository data and updates among replica servers?

relations.rationale: Coordinated reference transactions create a need to verify that replicas retain equivalent logical state.

values.label: Application-level repository replication
values.description: Applying repository replication in an application-level system rather than filesystem replication.

values.label: Git-and-rsync replication mechanisms
values.description: Combining Git and rsync mechanisms to replicate repository content.

values.label: Orchestrated packfile fan-out
values.description: Distributes pushed packfiles to every repository instance before references are published.

values.label: Unsynchronized packfile distribution
values.description: Fans out unreachable packfiles without consensus, relying on later synchronized reference commitment.

values.label: Packfile-level replication
values.description: Replicates Git data as packfiles while leaving Git operations standard on each repository replica.

values.label: Fully consistent replica synchronization
values.description: Keeps replicated Git data synchronized so clients and CI can immediately read newly pushed commits.

values.label: Repository-consistency complexity cost
values.description: Incurs substantial operational complexity to keep repository copies fully synchronized.

values.label: Optimistic UDP gossip replication
values.description: Replicas exchange catch-up metadata through lossy gossip while authoritative reads verify state independently.

values.label: Direct S3 replica catch-up
values.description: Replicas retrieve WAL indexes and data directly from object storage rather than transferring state replica-to-replica.

values.label: Idle-replica removal and rematerialization
values.description: Inactive repository replicas are removed from disks and recreated from the authoritative WAL when needed.

values.label: S3 distribution of compacted packs
values.description: Replicas download already-compacted packs from object storage instead of performing local repacking.

values.label: Linear read scaling across replicas
values.description: Adding replicas increases read-serving capacity approximately linearly without reducing push throughput.

clusters.name: Replica Update Scheduling
clusters.description: How are competing repository updates prioritized and coalesced?

relations.rationale: Coordinated reference transactions create a need to verify that replicas retain equivalent logical state.

values.label: Coalesced bookkeeping reference updates
values.description: Combining non-time-critical bookkeeping reference updates into fewer transactions.

values.label: Priority scheduling for user-initiated updates
values.description: Prioritizing user reference updates over bookkeeping updates during cascades.

clusters.name: Replica Checksum Strategy
clusters.description: Which checksum implementation verifies equivalence among replicated repository states?

relations.rationale: Replica commit coordination produces state whose post-update equivalence must be checked independently.
Replica commit coordination produces state whose post-update equivalence must be checked independently.
Replica commit coordination produces state whose post-update equivalence must be checked independently.
Replica commit coordination produces state whose post-update equivalence must be checked independently.

values.label: Spokes checksum
values.description: Summarizes reference names, values, and replica state to compare logical contents across replicas.

values.label: Incremental XOR checksum maintenance
values.description: Updates checksum contributions when references change instead of rescanning the complete reference set.

values.label: Full checksum recomputation
values.description: Recomputing all reference hashes from scratch becomes expensive for repositories with many references.

values.label: Reference-update throughput constraint
values.description: The cost of full recomputation would limit the achievable rate of reference updates.

clusters.name: Repository Placement Strategy
clusters.description: Documents vary by how requests locate repositories and how missing local materializations are recovered across a changing server cluster.

values.description: Maps repository identifiers to expected nodes without maintaining authoritative placement state.

values.label: Repository-ID and healthy-node routing
values.description: Uses only the repository ID and current healthy-node set, tolerating stale routing because repositories can be rematerialized.

values.label: Rendezvous-ranked preferred primary
values.description: Normally favors the highest-ranked node to reduce compare-and-swap retries while allowing other servers during failures.

values.label: Any-replica read routing
values.description: Routes fetches and clones to any synchronized replica instead of a designated read replica.

values.label: Routing-database availability dependency
values.description: What dependency is introduced by storing repository-to-machine placement in an external routing database?

clusters.name: Maintenance Transition Strategy
clusters.description: Documents vary by how servers enter planned maintenance while preserving active reads and continued replicated writes.

relations.rationale: The maintenance procedure reuses replica coordination behavior while withdrawing a server from new reads.

values.label: Direct reboot or unplugging
values.description: Stops a server immediately, risking interruption and loss of progress for long-running reads such as large clones.

values.label: Quiescing period
values.description: Withdraws a server from new reads while allowing active operations to drain before reboot.

values.label: Continued write delivery during quiescence
values.description: Continues sending writes to the quiescing replica so it does not fall arbitrarily behind.

values.label: Long and variable quiescence duration
values.description: Maintenance duration may range from seconds to hours because active reads, especially large clones, are allowed to finish.

values.label: Rolling reboot testing
values.description: Tests failures through planned rack-scoped rolling reboots rather than random interruption.

values.label: Rack-scoped availability-zone maintenance
values.description: Reboots one rack at a time and bounds simultaneous reboots within that rack.

values.label: Bounded parallel server reboots
values.description: Limits concurrent reboots after quiescence to control maintenance disruption.

values.label: Increased same-day write-rejection risk
values.description: Reduced replication after sudden loss increases the chance that later writes are rejected.

iterations.explanation:
Consolidated 192 draft values across 23 dimensions (merge threshold 0.350, borderline band 0.400). Merged 5 near-duplicate values:
  - [Client Garbage-Collection Policy] "Foreground automatic garbage collection" → "Disabled automatic garbage collection"
  - [Client Filesystem and Status Monitoring] "Watchman-based filesystem monitoring hook" → "Watchman filesystem watching"
  - [Replica Topology and Factor] "Geographically localized Git transfer serving" → "Geographically localized replica reads"
  - [Client Clone Materialization] "Virtualized filesystem materialization" → "Virtualized filesystem materialization"
  - [Client Clone Materialization] "Sibling build-output directories" → "Nested source working directory"
The remaining 182 values were distinct enough to keep as generated.
Evidence linking: 324 of 331 open codes assigned to a value (similarity >= 0.50); 48 of 48 documents now support at least one value.

values.description: Repository unavailability directly reduces developer and CI productivity.

clusters.name: Replica Topology and Factor
clusters.description: How many replicas and what physical topology provide repository redundancy and failure isolation?

values.label: Rack-level replica anti-colocation
values.description: Placing repository replicas in different racks to isolate rack-wide failures.

values.label: Distant replica placement
values.description: Placing replicas across geographically separated locations despite inter-replica latency.

values.label: Colocated filesystem replicas
values.description: Keeping filesystem replicas near one another because block replication is latency-sensitive.

values.label: Block-level filesystem replication
values.description: Replicating repository storage at filesystem or block level.

values.label: Three replicas per repository
values.description: Maintaining three repository copies as the selected replication factor.

values.label: Non-voting geo-replication replicas
values.description: Keeping geographically replicated hosts out of write-voting quorums so writes survive their temporary unavailability.

values.label: Elastic per-repository replica allocation
values.description: Replica counts vary with repository demand, from minimal availability to large read-serving pools.

values.label: Geographically localized replica reads
values.description: Serving reads from synchronized replicas near users to improve transfer locality.

values.label: Durable highly available content access
values.description: Maintaining durable, highly available repository and gist access through multi-copy replication.

values.label: Replication floor and capacity ceiling
values.description: The fixed replication floor is costly for small repositories while offering insufficient serving capacity for massive repositories.

values.label: Two-copy repository state after sudden loss
values.description: Leaves a repository with two surviving copies after an unexpected server disappearance, preserving service but reducing failure tolerance.

values.label: Replica-count scaling bottleneck
values.description: Increasing the number of replicas reduces push throughput under three-phase commit.

clusters.name: Authority Synchronization
clusters.description: Which mechanism coordinates authoritative repository state persistence and synchronization?

values.label: S3-backed write-ahead log
values.description: Persisting authoritative repository updates through a write-ahead log in S3.

values.label: S3 compare-and-swap synchronization
values.description: Uses atomic S3 compare-and-swap operations to serialize concurrent write-ahead-log updates.

values.label: WAL-based repository consistency
values.description: Uses a write-ahead log as the authoritative record for consistent repository operations without an external relational database.

values.label: Push acknowledgment after WAL persistence
values.description: Acknowledges pushes only after their complete operation is durable in the authoritative log.

values.label: Fully consistent repository views
values.description: Maintains every accessed repository view as fully consistent rather than partially consistent.

values.label: External relational database for repository references
values.description: Stores repository references in an external relational database alongside blob-stored packfiles.

values.label: Consensus-free repository primaries
values.description: Allows any server to receive updates instead of using elections or fixed primary ownership.

values.label: Repository copies as consensus source
values.description: What repository state establishes consensus for replicated operations?

values.label: Cloud-agnostic object-storage deployment
values.description: The authority log runs on S3-compatible object storage across cloud providers.

values.label: Batched WAL uploads
values.description: Multiple pushes are grouped to avoid one object-store write per push.

values.label: One-object-store-write-per-push ingestion
values.description: Each push is ingested with a separate object-store write.

values.label: Single-local-repository reference synchronization
values.description: Reference transactions synchronize with one local repository instead of a replica quorum.

values.label: Periodic WAL compaction
values.description: The write-ahead log is periodically compacted to bound restore cost and retained history.

values.label: Compaction results recorded across storage representations
values.description: Compaction outcomes are recorded for both the WAL and on-disk repository so replicas reproduce them.

values.label: S3 Express One Zone deployment
values.description: High-performance clusters use a lower-latency object-storage tier for WAL updates and push ingestion.

values.label: ETag-conditional read verification
values.description: Replicas use conditional object-storage reads to verify WAL-index freshness before serving fetches or clones.

clusters.name: Repository Serving Architecture
clusters.description: How does the application access repository storage across serving and storage nodes?

values.label: Stateless repository-serving cluster
values.description: Treats local repository copies as replaceable warm caches and avoids authoritative server-local repository state.

values.label: RPC-based repository access
values.description: Accessing repositories remotely through an application-facing RPC layer.

values.label: Dedicated repository fileservers
values.description: Storing repositories on dedicated fileservers rather than a shared distributed filesystem.

values.label: Co-located GVFS cache server
values.description: Places a cache server with the repository to handle many GVFS protocol requests.

values.label: Git protocol with Scalar registration
values.description: Uses ordinary Git protocol and client registration when GVFS cache infrastructure is unavailable.

values.label: GVFS without cache server
values.description: Uses GVFS protocol without a dedicated cache server for repositories small enough not to require one.

values.label: Horizontal application-server replication
values.description: How does the serving application scale its application instances around repository access?

values.label: Warm-cache materialization
values.description: Recreates absent local repositories from the S3 write-ahead log when routing directs work to another node.

values.label: Single-machine repository storage
values.description: Keeping each repository on only one machine after remote fileserver access.

values.label: Git hosting operational difficulty
values.description: Makes repository hosting operations a significant scalability and reliability concern.

values.label: Read-dominant repository workload
values.description: Operating under a workload with roughly one hundred reads per write.

clusters.name: Client Clone Materialization
clusters.description: How are repository content and working-tree data materialized on large-repository clients?

values.label: Partial-clone object materialization
values.description: Fetching missing repository objects on demand instead of storing every reachable object locally.

values.label: Virtualized filesystem materialization
values.description: Using a virtualized filesystem to support very large repositories without fully materializing content.

values.label: Sparse-checkout materialization
values.description: Populating only selected working-tree paths to control client materialization size.

values.label: GVFS-protocol cloning
values.description: Cloning through the GVFS hosting protocol for large repositories.

values.label: Nested source working directory
values.description: Places the working tree beneath the repository directory to separate source files from adjacent build outputs.

values.label: Reduced Git working-directory management load
values.description: Separating build outputs from the working directory reduces the work Git performs while managing repository files.

values.label: Reduced object-transfer burden
values.description: Partial transfer and caching reduce client data movement and central-server load compared with complete object database transfer.

values.label: Populated-file data cost
values.description: Populating working files costs substantially more data movement and processing than changing index entries.

values.label: Populated-file modification-detection cost
values.description: Determining modifications across many populated files becomes an important client scalability cost.

clusters.name: Repository Storage Representation
clusters.description: Which repository object representation and access pattern supports server-scale Git workloads?

values.label: Size-minimizing packfile layout
values.description: Organizing packed objects primarily to minimize storage size, accepting physical indirection and random reads.

values.label: Whole-file local caching
values.description: Caching an entire repository file locally to make random access acceptable.

values.label: Distributed filesystem architecture
values.description: Distributing repository storage through a shared filesystem.

values.label: Plain Git repositories on local NVMe
values.description: Stores ordinary Git repositories on local NVMe to support random packfile reads and standard client access.

values.label: Normal on-disk Git repository operations
values.description: Runs standard Git operations against ordinary on-disk repositories using upstream-compatible tooling.

values.label: Eventually consistent repository replicas
values.description: Allows replicas to expose newly pushed repository data only after propagation completes.

values.label: Content-addressable object storage
values.description: Repository objects are stored and addressed by content hashes.

values.label: DAG-dependent object traversal
values.description: Repository access follows dependent commit, tree, and file references sequentially.

values.label: Distributed key-value object storage
values.description: Git objects are mapped directly onto a distributed key-value store.

values.label: Distributed hash-table packfile storage
values.description: Normal on-disk packfiles are replaced by a distributed hash table.

values.label: Packfile-based network transfer
values.description: Git transfers repository changes through packfiles over the network.

values.label: Distributed identical repository instances
values.description: Hosting servers and developer machines retain the same distributed repository model.

values.label: Packfile-based repository storage
values.description: Repository code and metadata are stored in compressed filesystem packfiles.

values.label: Single on-disk HTTP repository
values.description: An HTTP daemon serves one local on-disk repository.

values.label: Server-internal non-packfile storage
values.description: The server uses an internal representation other than packfiles while preserving packfile network operations.

values.label: Multi-machine repository placement
values.description: Repository data is distributed across multiple disks and machines for parallelism and availability.

values.label: Efficient Git cloning
values.description: Preserves efficient cloning by retaining plain Git data rather than transforming it for clients.

values.label: Network-filesystem performance and correctness problems
values.description: What operational effect results when Git repositories are exposed through networked filesystem semantics?

values.label: Distributed-store access overhead
values.description: Object-level distributed storage adds repeated network round trips and latency.

values.label: Unacceptable clone performance
values.description: Object-level distribution makes repository cloning too slow for practical use.

values.label: Packfile hosting management burden
values.description: Large binary packfiles make filesystem-scale repository management difficult.

values.label: Packfile hosting scalability ceiling
values.description: Packfile-based hosting limits availability and scalability for large providers.

clusters.name: Packfile Lifecycle Management
clusters.description: How are Git packfiles repacked, indexed, retained, and removed over time?

values.label: Incremental pack-file repacking
values.description: Which pack-maintenance strategy limits each repacking operation while reducing large repositories’ pack count?

values.label: Multi-pack-index reference redirection
values.description: Which index mechanism redirects selected objects to newly generated packs while retaining old packs temporarily?

values.label: Deferred obsolete-pack deletion
values.description: When are obsolete pack files deleted relative to pack creation and reference updates?

values.label: Single-pack-file repacking
values.description: Accumulated packfiles are rewritten into one packfile as a maintenance strategy unsuitable for very large repositories.

values.label: Primary-only compaction
values.description: Only the primary replica performs repository compaction, while replicas consume the recorded result.

values.label: Replica-side repository repacking
values.description: Replicas independently trigger repository repacking as opposed to consuming primary-produced compacted data.

values.label: Unbounded pack-file accumulation
values.description: What pack-growth condition can result when pack maintenance is not bounded?

values.label: Pack-count and storage-footprint reduction
values.description: What storage result follows from incremental repacking and obsolete-pack expiration?

values.label: Git compaction as ingestion bottleneck
values.description: At high throughput, on-disk Git compaction becomes the limiting factor for repository ingestion.

clusters.name: Replica Failure Recovery
clusters.description: How are failed or retiring replica servers detected and repaired to restore repository redundancy?

values.label: Live-traffic-based failure detection
values.description: Detecting server failure from live application traffic and routing requests around unavailable servers.

values.label: Automated permanent-failure repair
values.description: Automatically restoring repository replication after disk or server failures.

values.label: Retiring-server replica-count removal
values.description: Removing a retiring server from active replica counts while keeping it available until repairs complete.

values.label: MxN failure-detection matrix
values.description: How are failure observations distributed across application servers and file servers?

values.label: Per-application-server failure isolation
values.description: How are failure classifications isolated when one application server has a local connectivity or DNS fault?

values.label: Heartbeat-based primary failure detection
values.description: Which mechanism is used as the primary detector for failed repository servers?

values.label: Advisory replica-offline status
values.description: How is an uncertain offline judgment represented in replica routing?

values.label: Cross-server fault inference
values.description: How are file-server faults distinguished from application-server faults?

values.label: Pet-style repository operations
values.description: Are repositories managed as individually irreplaceable assets or interchangeable instances?

values.label: Three-consecutive-failure offline threshold
values.description: A replica is marked offline only after three consecutive request failures.

values.label: Losing-replica isolation
values.description: Replicas on the losing side of a write vote are removed from reads and writes until repaired.

values.label: N-to-N replica reconstruction
values.description: Replacement replicas can be created anywhere from either surviving repository copy.

values.label: Localized failure-detector false positive
values.description: What failure-detection error can remain localized to one application server?

values.label: Operational burden of repository health management
values.description: What operational effect follows from continuous repository location, checksum, corruption, and repair management?

values.label: Cluster-size recovery scaling
values.description: Replica recovery accelerates as the file-server cluster grows.

values.label: Replica failover from concurrent maintenance
values.description: Concurrent maintenance on multiple replica nodes can trigger repository failover and availability impact.

clusters.name: Version-Control Operating Model
clusters.description: Which collaboration and repository-control model governs how users and teams exchange Git changes?

values.label: Distributed version-control model
values.description: Retains decentralized repositories and offline change exchange as the underlying version-control model.

values.label: Decentralized subsystem-maintainer workflow
values.description: Organizes development through many maintainers and decentralized subsystem ownership.

values.label: Offline work and delayed-push capabilities
values.description: Provides offline development and postpones synchronization with the central host.

values.label: Centralized repository hosting
values.description: Coordinates users through a centralized repository host despite distributed client capabilities.

values.label: Central-server-coupled object retrieval
values.description: Clients rely on a central server for missing objects, relaxing the fully distributed collaboration model.

values.label: Distributed-model mismatch with centralized workflows
values.description: Creates friction when organizations use centralized coordination rather than decentralized development.
